newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries supported in Tokyo before US data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries supported in Tokyo before US data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were well-supported by Tokyo midday on Tuesday, maintaining their bullish mood, traders said.
Activity was thin as the market waited for the release of U.S. consumer price index data and industrial production data due for release at 1230 GMT and 1315 GMT, respectively.

Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin's remarks saying the Fed will again face a "tough call" next month in deciding whether to raise interest rates further, slightly depressed prices in early trade, but follow-through sales were limited as prices quickly recovered from lows.
"The market was generally calm about Rivlin's comments as they were similar to her comments made last week," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 99-2/32, yielding 6.70 percent, compared with 99-3/32 in New York.
In New York on Monday, Treasuries rose for the third straight session due to continued bullish sentiment.

"The market is overbought, looking at the yield of the (6.25 percent) two-year note slightly breaking below the six-percent level," the trader said. "I don't expect it to sharply dip below that level."
Traders said that profit-taking may limit falls at the shorter end of the yield curve, while longer-end yields have more room to fall depending on the outcome of CPI data.
"Fading credit-tightening hopes are keeping the market undertone bullish. The 30-year bond yield could aim for 6.5 percent if such hopes were to intensify," another trader said.
Traders said Japanese investors are expected to limit their purchases until they determine the trend of the dollar after the G7 summit of industrialised nations in Denver this weekend.
Meanwhile, purchases from Europe are continuing to provide support to Treasuries, the first trader said.
The September T-bond futures contract rose 1/32 from the previous close to 112-3/32 by early afternoon trade. It was moving in a range of 112 to 112-6/32.
